title: The Optical Superhighway For AI
gist: Geoff Tate argues OCI-MSA, an optical scale-up consortium backed by AMD, Broadcom, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia and OpenAI, is the frontrunner standard for AI scale-up as copper gives way to optical within five years. He expects first Gen 1 implementations and interoperability demos in 2027.

insights.claim: Almost everyone agrees AI interconnects will move to all-optical over the next five years, though timing is disputed.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Sets the horizon for optical component and CPO supply-chain demand.
insights.quote: almost everyone agrees we are moving to all-optical interconnects over the next five years

insights.claim: Optical already dominates scale-out, will next enter scale-up by connecting racks in pods of hundreds to thousands of XPUs, and will then replace copper within the rack.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Defines the sequence in which optical content per AI system expands.

insights.claim: Pluggable transceivers mostly use single wavelengths over 2 or 4 fibers, so more bandwidth needs power-hungry faster PHYs or more fibers, which raises cost because connectors cost more than fibers.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Explains why pluggables hit a wall and why multi-wavelength approaches win.
insights.locator: Today, optical is dominated by pluggable transceivers

insights.claim: Industry consensus is shifting to multi-wavelength, bidirectional fibers using NPO and then CPO to cut power and cost while raising bandwidth.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Favors NPO/CPO vendors over pluggable-centric suppliers.

insights.claim: OCI-MSA is a consortium formed for an open, interoperable optical interconnect spec for AI scale-up, with founding members AMD, Broadcom, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia and OpenAI.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Both GPU giants, the top custom-AI-silicon maker and hyperscalers backing one spec makes it a strong bandwagon.

insights.claim: OCI-MSA aims to break proprietary interconnect constraints, guide the industry to low-power optical SerDes, and secure a multi-vendor AI supply chain without lock-in.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: An open standard threatens proprietary scale-up fabrics and favors multi-vendor supply.
insights.locator: The stated objectives for the OCI-MSA are

insights.claim: Meta's Drew Alduino said Meta wants AMD GPUs talking to Broadcom switches and all compute and switches interoperable.
insights.speaker: Drew Alduino
insights.so_what: Hyperscaler demand is the main driver of cross-vendor interoperability.
insights.quote: We want AMD GPUs talking to Broadcom switches
insights.locator: Drew Alduino (Meta's director of optical infrastructure)

insights.claim: Meta wants to standardize as little as possible for interoperability, wants OCI to look like Ethernet today, and says multi-wavelength means faster optical never requires faster SerDes.
insights.speaker: Drew Alduino
insights.so_what: Removing the SerDes speed treadmill lowers power and design risk.

insights.claim: OCI Gen 1 uses 8 wavelengths per fiber, 4 in each direction, each 53.125 Gbps NRZ (50 Gbps effective after error correction), spaced slightly over 2 nm, on a 500 m SMF-28 reference link with 2.5 dB total insertion loss.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Concrete Gen 1 parameters let suppliers plan interoperable products.

insights.claim: Gen 2 will double bandwidth and Gen 3 double it again, and 200G x 16 wavelengths has been shown viable, which is 16x Gen 1 bandwidth.
insights.speaker: Drew Alduino
insights.so_what: A clear roadmap argues OCI has long-term headroom.

insights.claim: Broadcom showed that at 200G aggregate one-way, OCI in CPO format has the best combination of low link power per bit and long reach, matching pluggable reach at one third of the power.
insights.speaker: Rajiv Pancholy
insights.so_what: Power per bit is the key economic argument for CPO in AI clusters; note the source is a Broadcom presentation.
insights.locator: At OCP (Open Compute Project) in October

insights.claim: AMD said OCI bandwidth can scale by more wavelengths (4 to 8, 16, 32), higher rates (50 to 400 Gbps), two polarizations and advanced modulation like PAM/QAM, for over 100x total scaling.
insights.speaker: AMD
insights.so_what: If OCI doubles every 1 to 2 years, it offers decades of runway.

insights.claim: Microsoft plans CPO on the switch and NPO at the accelerator in a first wave of scale-up optics, then CPO at both ends in a second wave.
insights.speaker: Microsoft
insights.so_what: Shows hyperscaler staged adoption timing for co-packaged optics.
insights.locator: Microsoft's first wave of scale-up optical

insights.claim: OCI-MSA is so far the only published optical scale-up standard frequently discussed at multiple conferences by multiple champions (AMD, Broadcom, Meta, Microsoft).
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Early standard momentum matters in interconnect winner-take-most outcomes.

insights.claim: The first fully functional OCI Gen 1 implementations, and perhaps supplier interoperability demos, are likely in 2027.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: A 2027 catalyst date for optical scale-up supply chain news.

insights.claim: If a bandwagon forms with multiple suppliers, OCI could become the Ethernet of optical interconnects, though other standards could emerge or some players may go proprietary.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Proprietary optical fabrics remain a risk to the open-standard thesis.
